To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in extremely shallow quantum well structures, the Coulombic coupling of confined states to quasi-continuum (or continuum) states leads to a transition from a two-dimensional to a three-dimensional electroabsorptive effect, and this transition occurs at a critical AlAs mole fraction in the barriers that is much smaller than the AlAs mole fractions at which the exciton states become quasi-two-dimensional in conventional quantum wells.

the transition from two-dimensional to 3D electroabsorption is observed at AlAs mole fractions much lower than 0.01 in extremely shallow quantum well structures, and that this behaviour is strongly dependent on the strength of the electric field.

the transition from red to blue shifts with applied electric field in the absorption edge of an extremely shallow quantum well is observed at an AlAs mole fraction as small as 0.003, and that Coulombic coupling of different subband pair states is essential for an accurate prediction of the behaviour of the absorption edge in extremely shallow quantum well systems.

the transition from red to blue shift in the absorption edge with electric field is not a general feature of shallow quantum wells, but depends on the strength of the confinement.
in extremely shallow quantum well structures the Coulombic coupling is strong enough that the absorption edge behaviour is not determined by the lowest energy transition.
